opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Research, engineering and running the business side of the fabs — TSMC reports this as one line in its earnings release.

follow100Note: For every $100 TSMC took in, $48.35 survived as profit. AI data-center chips (high-performance computing) supplied $55 of the $100 — and advanced nodes (7-nanometer and below) made up 77% of wafer revenue. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: TSMC reports in New Taiwan dollars (revenue NT$1,046.1B; net income NT$505.7B). Dollar figures are converted at NT$31.01 per US$1 — implied by TSMC's own stated US-dollar revenue of $33.73B. Operating expenses are shown as one line, as in TSMC's earnings release, and segment dollars apply the platform percentages from TSMC's official earnings presentation to total revenue. The tax line is set so the flow lands on net income attributable to TSMC shareholders.
otherDetail: Non-operating income of NT$27.5B (about $0.9B) — mostly interest earned on TSMC's large cash pile.

segments.name: Smartphone
segments.note: Chips for phones — a seasonal jump in the December quarter.

segments.name: Internet of Things

takeaways.text: 3-nanometer chips were 28% of wafer revenue, 5-nanometer 35% and 7-nanometer 14% — more than three-quarters of sales come from advanced nodes rivals still cannot match at scale.
takeaways.title: Leading edge is the business

takeaways.text: A gross margin of 62.3% and a net margin of 48.3% mean nearly half of every revenue dollar became profit — even while TSMC builds new fabs on three continents.
takeaways.title: Margins near record levels

takeaways.text: TSMC set its 2026 capital budget at $52–56B and guided first-quarter 2026 revenue to $34.6–35.8B, with gross margin of 63–65%.
takeaways.title: A record building budget

verdict: TSMC's revenue rose 21% to NT$1,046.1B ($33.7B) on strong demand for its most advanced chips — and with a 62.3% gross margin, it kept NT$505.7B ($16.3B) as profit, up 35% in a year.
